newsitem.title: PERU: Peru president's rating dips to 60 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru president's rating dips to 60 pct - poll.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's public approval rating dipped to 60 percent at the start of September from 62 percent a month earlier, a leading pollster said late on Sunday.
The survey of 500 Lima residents by Peruvian pollster Apoyo S.A. also showed 48 percent agreed Fujimori could stand for a third consecutive election, while 42 percent disagreed.
While Fujimori is mulling a possible third election bid in 2000, opposition parties are calling for a referendum to decide whether he can legitimately stand again.
Last month, the government-controlled Congress voted in favor of a constitutional interpretation that allows the president's re-election.
Under Peruvian law, a president who has been elected for two consecutive terms in office is not allowed to run in the following election.
Since taking office in 1990, Fujimori has held relatively high popularity ratings due to his virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reforms and strong leadership.
The margin of error in the latest Apoyo survey -- announced on national television -- was not available. Normally the monthly survey has a five percent margin of error.
